The hurricane causing most damage (economic) in Harrisburg was Hazel (October 15, 1954) bringing gusts of wind up to 80 miles per hour (mph). Although tornadoes are fairly common in Pennsylvania the only tornadic winds observed in Harrisburg have been connected with severe thunderstorms, rather than the funnel-type vortices.

g. The River
(1)General
A discussion of the City of Harrisburg would be incomplete without mention of the Susquehanna River and its influence on the City. Not only is the River the most outstanding geographic element of the City (the City limits extend to the western shore of the river) but it is also the reason for the City's development at this point on the map. Before settlement of the area by Europeans, American Indians used rocks that extended from the river bed to ford the river in the vicinity of the southern end of the project area. John Harris, the first settler and for whom the city is named, established a ferry along side these rocks in 1733. Subsequently, his ferry operation and trading post developed into what is now the City of Harrisburg.
